editions.text:
The Tufted Titmouse arrived two minutes before sunrise, maintaining a steady rhythm of visits until nearly two hours after light. By 07:43, a Carolina Chickadee joined the rotation, while the Northern Cardinal dominated the early auditory landscape with twenty-two detections in the seventh hour.

The first confident visual record of a House Finch at this station came when an adult male perched on the top ring of the metal stand.

By 10:30, seventy visits had been recorded, more than double the recent average of thirty-four. Thirteen species were accounted for, surpassing the usual seven.

The afternoon air holds at 27.2 C with a light 6 kph wind. Tufted Titmice remain the primary visual presence, with fifty-one confident visits logged so far, while Carolina Chickadees and American Crows round out the top seen counts. The first confident visual record of a Mourning Dove was confirmed.

Auditory detections show a shift in dominance since the morning edition. Northern Cardinals lead with ninety-five detections, closely followed by Blue Jays at fifty and Carolina Wrens at forty-nine.

By 15:30, the station has recorded one hundred and ten visits, more than double the recent average of forty-two. Fifteen species have been accounted for, exceeding the usual eight and a half.
